images.name: 余烬·偏蚀
images.design: Crimson-red ECLIPSE CLEAVER. Very broad asymmetrical continuous cleaver blade with a huge eccentric circular cutout occupying the middle third, bounded by a thick crescent cutting rim on the left and a straight broad heavy spine on the right. The round opening is cut THROUGH the solid blade, not a ring mounted as ornament. A small offset ruby energy disc levitates within the circular opening, visibly not concentric. Above the opening, a long angular guillotine point; below it, two step-cut shoulders smoothly join the hilt. Lower blade remains broad and feels heavy; overall a greatsword, not an axe or staff. Guard is a short angular crescent saddle pointing upward on one side, counterbalanced by a square block on the other. Deep ruby planes, red and slight coral rim emission. Sparse tiny red circular sparks around the offset inner disc. Do not use a row of triangles, multiple rectangular windows, or multiple floating blade segments.

images.name: 流萤·逐翎
images.design: Jade-to-mint LAMELLAR FIN greatsword. A wide straight central tapered sword spine, flanked by exactly FIVE broad backward-swept geometric blade fins on ONLY the left edge, each fin curves slightly and overlaps the next like sculpted aerodynamic louvers. The fins are long substantial sharpened slabs, lower two wider and more sweeping, upper fins progressively smaller, ending in one spear point. The right edge is a clean uninterrupted sharpened straight bevel. This creates a feather-like silhouette entirely out of solid geometric slabs, no literal feathers or organic texture, no spikes on both sides. Each layer is offset in depth, with thin dark channels between layers and mint rim lighting showing the three-dimensional stacking. Guard is two flattened overlapping crescent fins swept back toward the grip, asymmetric but compact; long straight grip and small flattened teardrop geometric pommel. Emerald green faces with turquoise and mint edges, a few tiny pale green chevron motes flowing diagonally backward. Avoid a forked blade, branch antlers, a hollow rectangular frame, or disconnected floating shards.

images.name: 寒汐·折矩
images.design: Cobalt-blue to cyan FOLDED RULER colossal greatsword. A SINGLE continuous massive broad rectangular blade slab folded into a shallow three-dimensional Z along its LENGTH: lower quarter tilts slightly right, broad middle offsets left, upper third returns right, joined by two thick bevelled angular elbow transitions. The blade stays upright and functional, not an L-shaped weapon. The entire edge is continuous, solid and sharpened, NO hollow windows and NO separate rings or floating pieces. A very long clean chamfered acute wedge tip, a subtle narrow cyan seam traverses each fold, broad darker blue planar faces make the spatial offset visible. Blade is about 5 times wider than handle and thick enough to communicate weight. Guard resembles a solid low T-beam with one stepped end and one oblique end, unlike a conventional symmetric cross. Straight long two-handed handle with a compact cuboid counterweight pommel. Four or five tiny cyan rectangular particles shed from elbow transitions. Strong minimalist brutalist monument silhouette. Avoid hammer heads, rectangles linked in a chain, ice crystals, circuitry and thin wire outlines.

images.name: 梦隙·回旋
images.design: Violet-to-lavender TWISTED DOUBLE-EDGE greatsword. Two wide solid blade ribbons twist around one another through exactly one graceful half-turn along the blade length, leaving a long narrow twisted almond-shaped negative space between them, and merge into ONE long unified spear-sharp tip. Show actual three-dimensional torsion: lower ribbon presents its broad face while upper opposite ribbon turns edge-on and then broadens. Thick clean faceted ribbon slabs with alternating deep plum, blue-violet and lavender luminous bevels, not rope, not a drill bit, not a coil with many turns. The outer overall silhouette is a straight tall double-edged greatsword, with a slight elegant bulge through the middle. Guard is a single diagonal open rhombus loop with its corners bent in depth to echo the blade twist, surrounding a small solid central hilt collar; usable long straight two-hand grip. Pommel a small flattened twisted lozenge. A few short curved violet particle arcs hug the central opening. No disconnected floating blade fragments, no crown, no jewel-encrusted metal, no hexagram.
